text: Steel spoon, wooden spoon. Same temperature. So why is steel ice cold?
Try it right now. Touch something metal, then something wooden.
A thermometer says they are exactly equal. Your hand disagrees.
Because your skin does not feel temperature. It feels heat leaving you.
Metal is a heat highway. It pulls warmth out of your finger, fast.
Wood is full of tiny air pockets. Heat barely moves, so it feels warm.
Same reason a tiled floor bites your feet, but a rug feels cozy.
Now the twist. In the hot sun, a metal bench burns you. Wood does not.
Now heat rushes in, just as fast. Your hand is fooled both ways.
Did you just touch a spoon? Comment yes or no.
